title: Taika Waititi Confirms His ‘Star Wars’ Movie Has Been Put ‘on Ice’ Indefinitely
description: Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his late
body:
Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.”

	“I hate to break this to you, but we’re going to actually put it on ice and we’re working on a different thing together,” Waititi told Inverse while discussing “Star Wars.” His publicist reportedly told him not to say more about it during the conversaiton. “Well, there’s your answer,” Waititi said. “I don’t even know how to dress it up or make it even vague.” “It’s very iced. I’ve got about four other movies I’m trying to do,” he continued. “Ice ages do come to an end… Who knows?”
	

	Back in Jan., the director had said he was “trying to go back and harness a little bit more of the fun from the original films, which is what I remember [from] them.”


	“The stakes are very high, and there’s serious things going on, but there’s also a lot of fun to be had in those films. That’s what I was trying to bring back,” Waititi continued. “I was trying to work in a world that was a little bit separate to that because they’ve got so many things going on within that space. For me to do something there, it would need to be a little different and a little bit more its own thing.”

	Previously, exiting Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy said Waititi’s “Star Wars” was “still somewhat alive.”

	Thus far, Waititi’s latest directorial effort, “Klara and the Sun,” has met a mixed response from critics and fans. Variety’s Guy Lodge wrote in his review that “Jenna Ortega tries hard to illuminate this misbegotten Kazuo Ishiguro adaptation, but Waititi’s decision to play it for strained, whimsical comedy is ruinous.”

schema.headline: Taika Waititi Confirms His ‘Star Wars’ Movie Has Been Put ‘on Ice’ Indefinitely

title: Inde Navarrette on Meeting Pamela Anderson, Hosting ‘SNL’ and X-Men Stunt Training
description: “Obsession” star Inde Navarrette had quite the busy weekend, going from the Academy Museum Gala on Saturday to the Newport Beach Film Festival on S
body:
“Obsession” star Inde Navarrette had quite the busy weekend, going from the Academy Museum Gala on Saturday to the Newport Beach Film Festival on Sunday.

	Navarrette attended the festival, which runs until Thursday in Newport Beach, as one of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch, who were celebrated during the festival’s Honor Brunch.

	While speaking with Variety’s Marc Malkin at the festival’s carpet, Navarrette said attending the gala was “amazing.” “I mean, you’re just overwhelmed and kind of drowning in everybody that you have looked up to, possibly ever, and it’s just so lovely meeting people and the reception that ‘Obsession’ has been getting… I’m just so honored to go and be with the members of the Academy and just get an inside scoop on what that magnificent world is like.”
	

	Jessica Lange and Pamela Anderson were two of the actresses Navarrette was excited to see Saturday night. “I spoke to Jessica Lange, who is an icon,” she said. “[And] the way that Pamela carries herself with such grace and honesty and just pure creativity and love is just exactly who I want to be.”

	And Navarrette’s schedule isn’t slowing down just yet — she’s set to host this year’s “Saturday Night Live” Halloween episode with musical guest Gracie Abrams. 

	“I literally I feel like I snuck in,” joked the actress. “I’m super excited to keep everything under wraps because I really truly want to make this super fun for the audience. And what I love is when I don’t know anything. So I’m really excited to be working with the writers.”
	

	Also on the horizon is the MCU’s forthcoming “X-Men” film, in which she’ll play Rogue. Navarrette told Malkin she hasn’t corresponded directly with Anna Paquin, who originated the role, but feels “the correspondence started when I was younger, when I really fell in love with the ‘X-Men’ movies in the first place.”

	On the topic of stunt training for the superhero film, Navarrette said it’s a good excuse to get herself in the gym. “I’ve always wanted to take part in that sort of a thing,” she said. “I think it’s also a really good excuse to get in the gym. I’m the laziest person, and I am very excited to get up and move my body.”

schema.headline: Inde Navarrette on Meeting Pamela Anderson, Hosting ‘SNL’ and X-Men Stunt Training

title: ‘The Simpsons’ Surprise: Apu Is Heard for the First Time in Nearly a Decade, as Sunil Malhotra Takes Over for Hank Azaria (EXCLUSIVE)
description: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of “The Simpsons,” “The Revengening,” which aired Sunday night on Fox.
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of “The Simpsons,” “The Revengening,” which aired Sunday night on Fox.

	“The Simpsons” has pulled off its own October surprise: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon is back. The fan favorite character finally spoke again for the first time in nearly a decade on Sunday night’s episode, “The Revengening.” Variety has exclusively learned who is behind Apu’s new voice: actor and voice-over vet Sunil Malhotra (“Grey’s Anatomy,” “The Legend of Korra”).
	

	Malhotra’s hiring and the return of Apu — who has been seen, but not heard on “The Simpsons” since the October 2017 episode “The Serfsons” — was a closely guarded secret inside “The Simpsons” universe. Fox didn’t share a screener for “The Revengening,” and producers kept both the episode’s table read and its subsequent production under tight protocols (including NDAs for all involved).


	Also heard on Sunday’s episode was the debut of Janina Gavankar (“The Morning Show”) as Apu’s wife, Manjula. And now that Apu is back and the Kwik-E-Mart has reopened, executive producer Matt Selman said both characters and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will once again be seen (and heard) on “The Simpsons” more often.

	“We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, ‘Simpsons’-y way that allowed him to evolve,” Selman said. “We’re excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future.”

	Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu, a character that has been controversial over the years due to its stereotypical portrayal of a South Asian convenience store clerk. The issue of Apu was the centerpiece of the 2017 documentary “The Problem With Apu,” in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent.
	

	After that doc made waves — including in “The Simpsons” writers’ room, where it was screened and discussed — Azaria announced that he would no longer voice Apu. “I apologize for my part in creating that and participating in that,” Azaria said in 2021 on Dax Shepard’s podcast “Armchair Expert.” “Part of me feels like I need to go to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologize. And sometimes I do.”

	In the aftermath, Apu was shifted to the background on “The Simpsons,” as producers decided how to handle the character going forward. For years, that meant Apu would still occasionally be seen in Springfield, but never heard.

	Until now. The idea of bringing back Apu this way, as one of this year’s Halloween-themed episodes, came from staffer Nick Dahan (who’s the credited writer on “The Revengening”) and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos. After hearing their pitch, Selman said he thought it was “a brilliant way” to bring Apu back and reference the entire situation. 

	Voice actor Malhotra said he took time to look into what it would mean to take over Apu and talked to the producers to make sure the character was more culturally appropriate.

	“When my agent called me about a ‘Simpsons’ audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink,” he said. “But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers’ room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes? Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably ‘Simpsons’ way that didn’t disappoint fans?

	“Whether the producers knew it or not, I was prepared to walk away,” he continued. Malhotra said that he declined his very first “professional job offer 28 years ago” because it would have required him to play a stereotypical “Hindu guy,” adding that playing such a caricature “to be the butt of the joke wasn’t something I was willing to do, and I’ve turned down similar work multiple times since.”

	But as Malhotra got further down the road with “The Simpsons,” he said, he began engaging with the producers about their plans for Apu before he would commit to the role, where he was promised that the return of Apu was being handled with the utmost care.
	

	“My callback was the first of many times that no one at ‘The Simpsons’ let me down,” he said. “I told casting that I’d only consider an offer if I could meet showrunner Matt Selman and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos, both of whom gladly did so. It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of ‘The Simpsons’ and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way.”

	In “The Revengening,” a spooky lead-up to next week’s “Treehouse of Horror XXXVII,” a man in a “Daft Monk” Halloween costume (as in, a Daft Punk helmet and monastic robe — wordplay!) is accidentally killed over and over again by Springfield residents all over town. A year later, “Daft Monk” is still alive, and getting his revenge by taking out his would-be killers, one by one.

	Eventually “Daft Monk” summons the townspeople to Springfield City Hall, where he takes his helmet off and reveals that he’s actually Apu.

	“I’d be lying if I didn’t say that the sweetest part of all was unleashing that righteously rage-fueled “I AM APU!” — on behalf of so many of us — over and over in the studio until we got it just right,” Malhotra said. “I really feel like we did and I can’t wait for fans to see more Apu.”

	Apu then shares his backstory: After he was nearly killed dozens of times, he wound up on “The Island of Forgotten Garbage,” where he’s healed by “The Simpsons” quack Dr. Nick (who also has been seen sparingly in recent years, and is now voiced by Eric Lopez, who previously also took over as Bumblebee Man). 

	“All the junk Springfield gets rid of winds up here,” he tells Apu, “like you … If you wound up here, it’s for a reason, right, Leon?” (Out pops the character that Michael Jackson played in the Season 3 episode “Stark Raving Mad,” which was pulled from “Simpsons” rotation in 2019 after the doc “Leaving Neverland” showcased more allegations against the late pop star.)

	Says Apu before he reveals himself: “I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed!”

	Then, unmasked, he tells the Springfield crowd: “It would have been so easy to bring me back. I immediately ran home to my family, but they were gone. Then I went to the Kwik-E-Mart, and was shocked to find it abandoned. As I wandered aimlessly through town, no one even noticed me. It was as if I was invisible. That was when I vowed to take my revenge on Springfield.”
	

	He’s about to light City Hall on fire, but Marge Simpson pipes up — representing the Springfield citizens, but also clearly serving as a mouthpiece for the show’s producers: “Apu, we’re so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, we wanted to do the right thing.”

	Bart adds: “But we were so scared, and just didn’t know what to do.”

	Lenny also chimes in, in a nod to the debates inside “The Simpsons” writers’ room: “If it’s any consolation, we had so many internal conversations about it.”

	But, Carl finishes, “Ahh, they kind of just didn’t go anywhere.” (And for almost a decade, that’s how “The Simpsons” never got around to bringing back Apu.)

	Homer then offers to sacrifice himself to save the rest of the town, and offers this penance to Apu, while reminding viewers how important Apu has been to the makeup of Springfield: “I’m just doing what the old Apu would have done. The guy who loved this town and everyone in it. You were on our bowling teams, our barbershop quartets, our dad rock cover bands. We took you for granted. I took you for granted.”

	But before Apu can blow up the town, he wakes up. It turns out it was a nightmare; no one is dead. He’s back in the Kwik E-Mart, and Manjula is there too. So is his No. 1 customer, Homer, who invites him to a Halloween party.

	“What the heck? I’ll do it,” Apu says. “A Halloween party sounds kind of fun. Plus, I feel like I haven’t seen everyone in ages. Oh, but I wish I had a costume.”

	But he actually does: There’s a “Daft Monk” costume stashed under the cash register. So was it really a dream? And that’s the end of the episode — but Apu is back!

	This isn’t the first time “The Simpsons” writers used their characters to allude to their indecisiveness on what to do with Apu. In the 2018 episode “No Good Read Goes Unpunished,” Marge begins reading her favorite childhood novel to Lisa, but quickly realizes the old book was a lot more offensive and racist than she remembered. She tries to sanitize it, but “now it’s as inoffensive as a Sunday in Cincinnati … what am I supposed to do?”

	Lisa then looks at the audience, seemingly addressing “Simpsons” fans: “It’s hard to say. Something that started decades ago and was applauded and inoffensive is now politically incorrect. What can you do?”
	

	The scene pulls back to reveal a photo of Apu near Lisa’s bed, and it’s obvious they’re no longer talking about a book, but their own show. With Marge also looking straight at viewers, the two suggest that “Some things will be dealt with at a later date … if at all.” (It should be noted that Apu and his children also appeared in the episode, but did not speak.)

	In June 2020, during the post-George Floyd reckoning on race, “The Simpsons” announced that moving forward, its characters of color would be voiced by culturally appropriate actors. Among the major changes, Alex Désert took over as Carl Carlson from Azaria, and Kevin Michael Richardson (who had already been a part of the series cast) became Dr. Julius Hibbert, which was previously Harry Shearer. Now, Apu, with Malhotra taking over, joins that list as well.

	And for several years, the creative team promised that they would address Apu at some point. In 2021, series creator Matt Groening told USA Today that the producers were first seeing if they could make new Apu stories work. “I think the Apu stories are fantastic, and he’s one of the most nuanced characters on a silly two-dimensional cartoon show,” Groening said in the interview.

	Early reactions on social media about the return of Apu has already been positive: “Apu is back thank you Simpsons,” said one. Another: “The Simpsons reveals the new voice for Apu. Representation for Indian Americans. Well played Matt Groening and Dan Castellaneta, Hank Azaria, Nancy Cartwright, Harry Shearer, Julie Kavner and Yeardley Smith.” Wrote a third: “Apu reveal is the greatest thing to happen on the Simpsons in a long time. I missed that genius character!”

	Meanwhile, Malhotra and Gavankar jointly posted this reveal on their Instagram pages:


	Malhotra’s recent voice credits include “The Legend of Vox Machina,” “The Loud House,” “Monster High,” “The Casagrandes” and “Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi.” He’s also been heard on video games including “Mortal Kombat 1,” “Avatar: The Last Airbender – Quest of Balance” and “Marvel’s Avengers.” In TV, besides “Grey’s Anatomy,” he’s also appeared on “ER,” “NCIS: New Orleans,” “MacGyver” and “Maron.”

schema.headline: ‘The Simpsons’ Surprise: Apu Is Heard for the First Time in Nearly a Decade, as Sunil Malhotra Takes Over for Hank Azaria (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Glee’ Reunion: Chris Colfer Joins Darren Criss Onstage to Perform ‘Baby It’s Cold Outside’ During London Concert
description: Darren Criss‘ one-night-only concert at the Royal Albert Hall in London became a “Glee” reunion when the singer surprised audiences by bringing out
body:
Darren Criss‘ one-night-only concert at the Royal Albert Hall in London became a “Glee” reunion when the singer surprised audiences by bringing out Chris Colfer and performing “Baby It’s Cold Outside” as an homage to their characters on the hit show, Kurt Hummel and Blaine Anderson.

	Criss began the song solo, telling the audience he’d be singing both parts, even though “it’s not supposed to be like that, but I’ve managed to pull off so many things,” he said, before Colfer joined him a few verses later. “The only thing inappropriate about doing this song is doing it without me,” joked Colfer before he began singing.
	

	Criss and Colfer first performed the song during the Season 2 Episode 10 titled “A Very Glee Christmas,” which aired in 2010. Their characters were fan favorites who began dating in Season 2 before getting engaged and married in the final season.


	Last month, following long-swirling rumors of a potential “Glee” reboot, creator Ryan Murphy officially weighed in and revealed there’s a script. “Well, funny you ask, ’cause I just finished the script an hour ago,” Murphy told Entertainment Tonight. “So, we have a script. Brad [Falchuk], Ian [Brennan] and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something. I’ve been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members. It’s very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”

	Murphy noted that although there is a script, “nobody’s read it.” “So I don’t know, we’ll see,” he continued. “I vowed to myself that I wanted to write a couple of them to see what people think, particularly the cast, ’cause we were very close when we were making it.”
	

	“Glee” first premiered in Sept. 2009, and in addition to Michele, Colfer and Criss, it starred Corey Monteith, Naya Rivera, Dianna Agron, Matthew Morrison, Jane Lynch, Heather Morris and more.

schema.headline: ‘Glee’ Reunion: Chris Colfer Joins Darren Criss Onstage to Perform ‘Baby It’s Cold Outside’ During London Concert

title: Katseye Says They’re ‘So Proud’ of Sophia Ahead of Her Return to the Group: ‘She’s Our Sister’
description: Katseye is excited to welcome Sophia Laforteza back to the group after a brief hiatus. Members Lara Raj, Daniela Avanzini, Megan Skiendiel and Yoon
body:
Katseye is excited to welcome Sophia Laforteza back to the group after a brief hiatus. Members Lara Raj, Daniela Avanzini, Megan Skiendiel and Yoonchae Jeung shared their support for their “sister” on the carpet at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show on Sunday. 

	“We are so happy that she’s coming back,” Raj told E! News, speaking for the group. “We are so proud of her. I think she’s really been so brave, and we respect her so much for taking the space and taking time for her health. She’s our sister, so we can’t wait for her to come back.”
	

	Laforteza announced in August that she would be taking a step back from upcoming promotional activities to prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” HYBE x Geffen confirmed earlier this month that Laforteza is scheduled to return to group activities beginning in January 2027.


	The girl group kicked off its “Wildworld” tour in Dublin on Sept. 1, with the first U.S. stop in Miami on Oct. 13. The tour continues across North America through the end of November, with shows in Boston, Montreal, Chicago, Los Angeles and Mexico City.

	Laforteza’s step back from the group comes after member Manon Bannerman announced her own temporary hiatus in February. There has been no announcement made about her return to the group.

	Katseye formed and gained popularity as K-pop trainees on the 2023 reality competition series “Dream Academy.” Their new documentary, “Katseye: Wild Hearts,” hit Disney+ and Hulu on Oct. 16. The film picks up where Netflix docuseries “Pop Star Academy: Katseye” left off, following the group on their journey to pop stardom after leaving the competition series.

schema.headline: Katseye Says They’re ‘So Proud’ of Sophia Ahead of Her Return to the Group: ‘She’s Our Sister’

title: Jason Sudeikis Hopes to Continue ‘Ted Lasso’ for Season 5, Says Coverage of Split From Olivia Wilde Missed a ‘Million Little Things’: ‘It’s Always More Complicated’
description: Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of “Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso,” discussing his hopes for “Ted Lasso” Season 5, how the show “saved” h
body:
Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of “Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso,” discussing his hopes for “Ted Lasso” Season 5, how the show “saved” him from “self-harm” and what the public got wrong about his closely followed 2020 split from ex Olivia Wilde.

	Sudeikis and Fragoso talked “Ted Lasso” up top, as the host asked whether the actor wanted to continue the show for Seasons 5 and 6. (The Season 4 finale aired earlier this month.) Sudeikis said he “would like to,” but the status of future seasons remains unknown: “Yeah, I just don’t know,” he said, assuring Fragoso he wasn’t being coy “intentionally.” “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that,” he noted. He added that he would “assume” Apple would continue the show if the main cast wanted to return.
	

	The former “Saturday Night Live” star also got candid about what “Ted Lasso” saved him from, as he’s mentioned on multiple occasions. “Some form of self-harm. Flat out,” Sudeikis answered, describing a feeling that he hadn’t felt since “the confusing teenage years.” “ That’s probably the rawest, most, maybe embarrassing, but I don’t think it’s embarrassing… It does bubble up shame in me to think like, ‘How dare you? How dare you have those kinds of thoughts,’ you know?” The actor continued to describe wanting to be a drummer or a dancer as a teen to get out his emotions. “So how did [‘Ted Lasso’] save me? To a certain degree, it helped [and] it carried me as sometimes the work has done in the past.”


	Sudeikis’s ex-fiancé, Olivia Wilde, also came up, as the host asked about what the “Ted Lasso” star feels the public coverage of their separation missed. (Sudeikis specifically made headlines in 2022 when Wilde was served with child custody documents during her appearance at CinemaCon.)
	

	“Oh, gosh. I mean, a million little things,” he responded. “But, but what’s interesting is that it allows you capacity for empathy for when others go through those. And you need not be as lucky as we are to get to do something that we love.”

	He continued: “I don’t wish it on anyone because I don’t think it really moves the needle. And to be clear, this isn’t like, all evil is just misunderstood or something like that. I just mean these, interpersonal situations that then get portrayed as being these binary situations of right and wrong… It’s always more complicated, more human than that.”

	Sudeikis praised Wilde’s work: “Olivia loves what she does and is very, very good at and always has been. I’m thrilled for her.” (The actress and director is in the middle of the Oscars conversation for her work on “The Invite.”)

schema.headline: Jason Sudeikis Hopes to Continue ‘Ted Lasso’ for Season 5, Says Coverage of Split From Olivia Wilde Missed a ‘Million Little Things’: ‘It’s Always More Complicated’

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ Spends 15th Week at No. 1 on Albums Chart
description:
Taylor Swift holds steady at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as “The Life of a Showgirl” spends a 15th non-consecutive week atop the chart.

	This week,
body:
Taylor Swift holds steady at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as “The Life of a Showgirl” spends a 15th non-consecutive week atop the chart.

	This week, “Showgirl” earned an additional 87,000 equivalent album units thanks to its “Encore” edition, which touted four new tracks including the Hot 100-topping “Patient Zero.”

	“Showgirl” was initially released in October 2025, moving a whopping 2.7 million copies in its opening frame. Swift released the “Encore” edition on September 24, collecting 173,000 equivalent units in its first week. Last Monday, “Patient Zero” held steady at No. 1 on the Hot 100 for a second week, marking Swift’s 51st career week at the top and giving her the fifth-highest total in chart history for weeks at No. 1 behind Mariah Carey (101), Rihanna (60), the Beatles (59) and Drake (58).
	

	The singer, meanwhile, has been performing at private events over the past few months, including an appearance at the Grammy Museum and a Ross House FYC showcase. Just last night, she gave her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala. Swift ran through songs including “I Knew It, I Knew You” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” as well as “Blank Space” and “Love Story.”

	Elsewhere on the Billboard 200, rock group Greta Van Fleet earned its fourth top 10 with their latest, “Palace for the People,” which bows at No. 9. Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” lands at No. 2, followed by Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 3, Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” at No. 4 and Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide” at No. 5. Drake’s “Habibti” lands at No. 6; Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” bumps to No. 7; Kahan’s “Stick Season” rises to No. 8; and Drake’s “Iceman” rounds out the top 10.

schema.headline: Taylor Swift’s ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ Spends 15th Week at No. 1 on Albums Chart

title: Joe Manganiello Says Ben Affleck’s Scrapped Batman Film Would Have Seen Deathstroke ‘Dismantle Batman’s Entire Life’ and Kill Commissioner Gordon
description: Joe Manganiello, who was set to reprise the role of Deathstroke in Ben Affleck’s scrapped Batman film, is telling all about what would have happene
body:
Joe Manganiello, who was set to reprise the role of Deathstroke in Ben Affleck’s scrapped Batman film, is telling all about what would have happened had the superhero film made it to theaters.

	In his new memoir “Bloodlines,” published on Tuesday, the actor wrote that Affleck, who was attached as the writer, director, producer and star, planned to make the film “a superhero version of David Fincher’s ‘The Game’” in which Deathstroke would “dismantle Batman’s entire life” after being made to think the Caped Crusader killed his son (via EW).
	

	Manganiello, who first played Deathstroke, a DC supervillain, briefly in 2017’s “Justice League,” wrote that murdering Commissioner Gordon, holding Alfred Pennyworth hostage and breaking into the Batcave would all be a part of Deathstroke’s revenge plan, and that the film would have included a fight in which “Deathstroke would nearly kill both Batman and Batgirl before they would both escape via an aboveground train.”


	According to the “Magic Mike” actor, the film would have concluded with a “climactic one-on-one showdown through the streets of Gotham.” “It sounded good to me,” Manganiello wrote. “I told Ben how great I thought his films were, especially ‘The Town,’ and how I was really looking forward to seeing his Best Picture version of a Batman movie.” He went on to explain that Affleck’s roles on set sounded like “a lot” for a single person, to which the “Argo” director responded: “Yeah, I know…But don’t worry, you’re in good hands. You’re in good hands, man.”
	

	Ultimately, the film never came out. Recently, Ben Affleck appeared on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast and called the “Justice League” reshoots the “low point of my career.”

	“The experience of ‘Justice League’ was so negative for lots of different reasons, some of which have to do with where I was at personally and some of which had to do with the tragedy that happened at that time,” Affleck said. “I saw how not to make a movie like that, which is where the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You are really making a mistake. I was really glad and gratified that Zack got to release [his version via the Snyder Cut]. That was fucking great. I was really happy for him. That was shitty, him being taken off that movie and the reshoots that we did. If you want the low point of my career, it was that.”

schema.headline: Joe Manganiello Says Ben Affleck’s Scrapped Batman Film Would Have Seen Deathstroke ‘Dismantle Batman’s Entire Life’ and Kill Commissioner Gordon

title: Julianne Moore Says ‘The Debut’ Is ‘One of the Best Scripts I’ve Ever Read’ as Jesse Eisenberg’s Musical Comedy Closes London Film Festival on a High Note
description: “The Debut” ended London Film Festival on a high note Sunday night as director Jesse Eisenberg and star Julianne Moore gushed over each other to a
body:
“The Debut” ended London Film Festival on a high note Sunday night as director Jesse Eisenberg and star Julianne Moore gushed over each other to a packed audience at the Royal Festival Hall.

	“I mean, this movie stars my favorite person, Julianne Moore,” Eisenberg began as the duo came onstage to introduce the musical comedy. “But ironically, strangely, it’s the story of my life.”

	Written and directed by Eisenberg, “The Debut” stars Moore as Mona Friedman, a shy New Jersey housewife who auditions for a part in her local theater’s production of a fictional musical called “Nosy Neighbors.” After she’s cast in the supporting role of Miss Danielle, Friedman’s life begins to unravel as she becomes more consumed with playing the part and falls under the spell of director Jerry Blankenbuehler (Paul Giamatti).
	

	Eisenberg said he started doing community theater when he was “7 years old and miserable,” and it changed his life forever. “I wanted to write about that experience in my life, but I could only picture Julianne, to the point where I was writing it and she was inspiring me,” he added. “It’s the most thrilling experience to watch her and edit her for two years.”


	Moore, wearing a chic black gown, returned the praise. She called “The Debut” an “incredible gift” and said it’s “one of the best scripts I’ve ever read in my entire life.”

	“It was such an honor to receive it and such a thrill to go to work every day and to get to do this incredible part with these tremendous actors,” she said, adding of Eisenberg: “He’s a beautiful writer, exemplary director and just a great talent.”
	

	In response, Eisenberg quipped: “I just want to note that the only time I’m called beautiful, it’s about writing.”

	“The Debut” team fully leaned in for the U.K. premiere, with each guest finding a fake Playbill for “Nosy Neighbors” at their seat. During the screening, there was plenty of audible laughter and several rounds of applause for high points in Moore’s campy performance. 


	Sadly, Eisenberg said that Giamatti could not attend as he has COVID-19. “I wish he could be here. He is the greatest guy and you would love to hear him talk,” he said. “Paul’s been my favorite actor since I’m young, Julianne’s been my favorite actress since I’m young.”

	Alongside Moore and Giamatti, “The Debut” also stars Eisenberg, Halle Bailey, Colton Ryan and Bonnie Milligan as actors in the musical. Bernadette Peters, Lilli Cooper, Maulik Pancholy and Havana Rose Liu round out the cast. 

	Of acting with his childhood heroes, Eisenberg said it was “the thrill of a lifetime” but also “very strange.”

	“I was spending so much time enthralled with them, and then it was like Michael Jordan said, ‘Here, you take the ball!’ And I’m like, ‘What is this thing?’ So it was so distracting to me. I hope to never act alongside them again,” he joked. “I was my worst self.”

	“The Debut” premiered at Telluride Film Festival last month, where it earned rave reviews and Oscar buzz for leading lady Moore. In Variety‘s review, chief film critic Owen Gleiberman wrote: “‘The Debut,’ a small-town-theater comedy rooted in big ideas, is a funny and dizzying mind-bender. It’s like ‘Waiting for Guffman’ made by the Coen brothers at their most rivetingly unhinged.”

	“The Debut” is set to hit theaters on Dec. 11 via A24.

schema.headline: Julianne Moore Says ‘The Debut’ Is ‘One of the Best Scripts I’ve Ever Read’ as Jesse Eisenberg’s Musical Comedy Closes London Film Festival on a High Note

title: Betty McGuire, ‘Growing Pains’ Actress, Dies at 100
description: Betty McGuire, the actress best known for her role as grandmother Kate Malone on the ABC sitcom “Growing Pains, died Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture &
body:
Betty McGuire, the actress best known for her role as grandmother Kate Malone on the ABC sitcom “Growing Pains, died Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture & Television Fund’s Wasserman Campus in Woodland Hills, Calif., of natural causes. She was 100.

	Keith Gerchak, McGuire’s POA, confirmed her death.

	McGuire had a seven-year run on “Growing Pains” as Kate Malone, mother to Joanna Kerns’ Maggie. She was a recurring character in Seasons 1-2 and again in Seasons 4-7.
	

	Aside from “Growing Pains,” McGuire’s career in television includes appearances in shows including “Falcon Crest,” “The Doris Day Show,” “Columbo,” “Star Trek: Deep Space Nine,” “Hill Street Blues,” “ER,” “CSI: Miami,” “MacGyver,” Moonlighting” and “Charlie’s Angels.”


	On the silver screen, McGuire appeared in feature films such as “Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke” and Michael Crichton’s “Coma.”

	The actress also performed with notable Broadway names including Ethel Merman, Barbara Cook, Bea Arthur and Tony Randall in original productions of “Plain and Fancy,” “Happy Hunting” and “Oh, Captain!” She headlined as “Mame” at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas and toured in productions of “Gypsy,” “Auntie Mame,” “Mame,” “Oliver!” “How to Succeed in Business…” and “The Ziegfeld Follies of 1956.”

	Later in life, McGuire volunteered as a receptionist and advocate at the Coalition for Economic Survival legal clinic in Los Angeles to offer support for low-income tenants facing eviction. She was an active resident of The Motion Picture & Television Fund Home. On Channel 22, the on-campus TV station at the retirement community, she hosted her own talk show, “GabFest.”
	

	McGuire has no survivors.

schema.headline: Betty McGuire, ‘Growing Pains’ Actress, Dies at 100

            A Catholic priest in Ecuador has died after a massive crucifix came crashing down on him in the middle of a church service ... and the terrifying accident was captured on a livestream.
      
    
      
      Catholic priest Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was killed when a crucifix fell on him during a service in Ecuador. Congregants tried to help, but he died from his injuries. https://t.co/u2b4DaZPok
              @Breaking911
          
  
    
            Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading Mass at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil on Saturday, when roughly 27 minutes into the livestreamed service the large wooden cross mounted behind the altar suddenly came loose and fell onto him.
      
    
            The service was being broadcast live online, and footage captured the shocking moment the crucifix toppled forward ... striking the priest near the altar as he addressed worshippers.
      

            The sudden collapse brought the service to an abrupt halt, with people inside the church reacting to the horrifying scene and rushing to help.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed Sánchez Molinari's death Sunday in a statement to Instagram, mourning the loss of the parish priest and offering condolences to his loved ones and fellow members of the religious community.
      
    
            Sánchez Molinari served as pastor of the church and was a member of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Catholic religious order.
      
    
            It's unclear what caused the heavy crucifix to detach from the wall. Church officials have not publicly provided an explanation for the collapse.

'SNL UK'
                          Hey Shane Gillis, Don't Call Women Whores You 'C***!!!'
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Shane Gillis is getting roasted across the pond ... with "Saturday Night Live UK" taking aim at the comedian following his latest controversial appearance on the OG show.
      
    
      
      ‘SNL’ (UK) takes a jab at Shane Gillis following his controversial ‘SNL’ (US) monologue.  https://t.co/7YoZHs5PrA
              @PopBase
          
  
    
            The British version of the sketch comedy series took a swipe at Gillis over his recent hosting gig … which made headlines after he used his opening monologue to call women in gyms “whores” and later accidentally dropped an uncensored F-bomb during a live sketch.
      
    
            "Weekend Update" host Ania Magliano reminded Shane he's not allowed to say the F-word on live TV, tagging the FCC guideline refresh with "you stupid f***ing c***."
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, Gillis let the expletive slip while playing the son of Cat in the Hat during an October 10 episode of 'SNL' -- immediately realizing his mistake and quickly apologizing at the end of the sketch saying "Sorry about earlier."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Actor Dan Levy previously called out Gillis on his monologue joke about women in gyms, calling it downright misogynistic.
      
    
            Gillis wasn't the only American 'SNL' star making waves overseas. James Austin Johnson, who plays President Donald Trump on the NBC show, made a surprise appearance on 'SNL UK' -- bringing his Trump impression to the British stage.
      
    
            Johnson's Trump crashed a sketch featuring British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, joking about a possible job swap with Burnham and taking shots at several British political and pop-culture stories.
      
    
            The crossover comes while the American 'SNL' is on a scheduled break, with the next new episode set for October 31, which will be hosted by "Obsession" star Inde Navarrette.
